questions.q: What in the EKF reacts first to GNSS interference?
options: The satellite count in the GPS message
questions.explain: Disagreement between GNSS and the inertial solution shows up first; the inertial sensors are immune to external interference.

questions.q: Satellites are normal and the accuracy is "excellent," but the EKF innovations are rising. This looks like:
options: The sky blocked by buildings and trees
questions.explain: The measurement contradicts the model despite a "good" fix.

questions.explain: 2 is AltHold, 3 is Land from all modes.

questions.q: What must the pilot always have when GPS degrades?
options: Non-GPS modes and the skill to fly them
RTL on a switch and a geofence around the site
questions.explain: A geofence and RTL are useless without position.

questions.q: How do you simulate GPS loss in SITL?
questions.explain: Before ArduPilot 4.7, SIM_GPS_DISABLE = 1. Other scenarios: SIM_GPS1_NOISE, SIM_GPS1_GLTCH_*, SIM_MAG1_OFS_*.

questions.q: What is the right transmitter power at a site?
questions.explain: Extra power jams your neighbors and heats the VTX.

questions.q: What does INAV do on a multicopter if GPS is lost during RTH?
options: Emergency Landing, since RTH needs position
Continues RTH on the last known heading and speed
questions.explain: If there is no position for longer than nav_position_timeout (5 s), INAV in RTH/WP switches to Emergency Landing: while an altitude estimate exists, the copter descends under speed control (nav_emerg_landing_speed) until the landing detector; failsafe_throttle is used only when there is no altitude either. failsafe_procedure is the response to RC loss, not GPS loss; a wing with inav_allow_gps_fix_estimation can continue the return on the estimate.
